chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī al-Walīd Ḥafṣ ibn Sālim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: When the muʾadhdhin says, “Qad qāmati al-ṣalāh,” should the people stand on their feet, or should they remain seated until their Imam comes?
He said: “No; rather, they should stand on their feet. Then if their Imam comes, otherwise the hand of a man from among the people should be taken and he should be brought forward.”

key_terms.الْقَوْمُ: the group or congregation present for prayer
key_terms.الْمُؤَذِّنُ: the one who gives the call to prayer
key_terms.فَيُقَدَّمَ: he is brought forward to lead
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: the phrase of iqāmah announcing that the prayer has begun

ai.seo_question: When the muʾadhdhin says “Qad qāmati al-ṣalāh,” should the congregation stand immediately or wait for the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling about the congregation at the time of iqamah. When the call “Qad qāmati al-ṣalāh” is pronounced, the people should stand, and if the designated Imam does not arrive, one man from among them should be appointed to lead the salat.
